title: Quarterly runway alignment for hosted API + model catalog (stitch & cadence)
creator: Aisha Rahman
description:
Purpose: create a single coordinated quarterly runway that aligns Hosted API releases and model catalog rotations with capacity hedges, evaluation gates, and OKR targets. This ticket defines the orchestration artifacts (timelines, gating criteria, canary windows, rollback triggers) and the stakeholder rhythm for Q2 deliveries.

Scope:
- Define commit windows for model lineup changes in hosted API (major swaps, variant promotions, quantized variants).
- Create gating checklist tied to evals (regression thresholds, latency delta thresholds, cost delta thresholds).
- Establish canary schedule and fallback lanes across regions/tiers.
- Map OKRs and initiative owners to milestones and decision owners.
- Coordinate with Dedicated and Private teams for capacity hedging and reserved pool planning.
- Draft runbook snippets for post-deploy regression triage and rollback.

Success criteria (acceptance):
- Published runway calendar with commit windows and canary windows in Confluence (link below).
- Gating checklist and regression guardrail thresholds agreed by Research/Runtime teams.
- Cross-functional signoff from Eng, DevEx, and Solutions by due_date.
- Canary automation hooks instrumented (feature flags and fallback policies) and a minimal dry-run executed in staging.

Artifacts & links:
- Planning doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Quarterly+Runway+Stitch+Q2
- Canary automation draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/repo/pull/4312
- Eval dashboard (latency / quality): https://dash.redwood.ai/d/hostedapi-evals/q2-runway

Notes on constraints and trade-offs:
- If model swap causes >10% latency increase on p95 in regional tier, prefer deferred rollout and canary expansion rather than immediate rollback to avoid churn.
- Cost delta guardrail set to +25% token-cost for first 2 weeks; beyond that requires exec approval.
- Strong preference for model-compatible fallbacks (quantized / smaller variant) over disabling endpoints for customer facing routes.

canary_plan_summary: Phase 1: internal traffic + smoke tests; Phase 2: 5% production traffic to low-risk customers (beta cohort); Phase 3: ramp to 100% with staged regional expansion. Rollback triggers: p95 latency >8% over baseline for 30m, hallucination rate regression >2% absolute, error rate increase >0.5% sustained 15m.
stakeholder_rhythm: Weekly runway sync — Tuesdays 09:00 PT (Eng PM Owners)
Milestone review — two checkpoints: pre-canary signoff (48h before), post-canary retrospective (72h after)
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Model regression in quality after quantized variant promotion. Mitigation: hold canary to beta cohort and enable auto-fallback to previous variant if hallucination threshold breached.
Risk: Capacity shortfall in Dedicated pools during ramp. Mitigation: pre-book burst capacity and stagger rollout by region; include finance-approved backstop commit.
Risk: Unexpected infra dependency (kernel scheduling). Mitigation: tie rollout to ENG-99201 merge; if delayed, postpone model swap to next commit window.
